facts.text: During the Revolutionary War, Continental troops built a fort on Marble Hill that the British seized and renamed Fort Prince Charles.
The New York Central and Hudson River Railroad opened Marble Hill station in 1905–1906, replacing the older Kingsbridge stop on the Spuyten Duyvil line.
Marble Hill’s small footprint belies a history of glacial rock, quarrying, and the 19th‑century canal that reshaped Manhattan’s edge.
Quarries along Spuyten Duyvil Creek mined marble that later appeared in landmarks such as the Statue of Liberty’s pedestal.
Because no firehouse existed, residents formed the Marble Hill Hose Company in 1895 to protect their neighborhood.
The first major residential project, Marble Hill Houses, opened in 1952, providing thousands of homes and shaping the area’s skyline.
